solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Leaving vessel for a quick break?

blocks.note: to be off is to be leaving
a cutter is a small sailing ship

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a boat to grab a short holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is from cricket: an off-cutter is a fast ball that cuts in from the off side when it hits the pitch, so it 'breaks' quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a ball that deviates off the pitch is said to break, and this delivery is bowled at pace, hence the question mark.

clue.text: One of biblical trio, I’ll be welcomed by padre without hesitation

indicators.note: a guest who is welcomed is taken inside, so one piece goes within the other
without means lacking, so the following word's letters are dropped

blocks.note: a padre is a priest, addressed as Father
the sound of a speaker hesitating
only the I counts; the contraction just makes the sentence read

explanation.surface: A clergyman speaking fluently tells someone they will be received into one of the virtues.
explanation.walkthrough: The trio is faith, hope and charity from St Paul's first letter to the Corinthians; 'without' drops letters before the I goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Faith, hope and charity are the three theological virtues named together in Corinthians, so faith is one of that biblical threesome.

clue.text: Teatime treat for Gill when spoiled (7, two words)

indicators.note: something spoiled is damaged and out of its proper shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: A cake intended for Gill at teatime is ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' reads as a preposition, but its letters are part of the mix. A fig roll is a British biscuit of fig paste in a soft pastry casing.
explanation.definitionFit: A fig roll is a biscuit commonly eaten with a cup of tea in the afternoon, a classic snack for that meal.

clue.text: Ancient tele needs adjusting with this – it makes a grumbling sound (12, two words)

indicators.note: something that needs adjusting is not yet in proper order, so these letters are to be reset

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
this points at the entry itself, which names the letter R

explanation.surface: An old television set needs fiddling with because it hums and growls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' refers to the answer itself: the canine letter is R, so R joins the other letters before the shuffle. R is so called because it sounds like a dog's growl.
explanation.definitionFit: R has long been called the dog's letter because its rolled sound resembles a dog snarling, a growl being a grumbling noise.

clue.text: Gin and tonic’s starter before chat

indicators.note: a starter comes at the beginning, so only the opening letter of the word is used
before tells us which piece is written ahead of the other

blocks.note: the first letter of tonic
to rap is to talk freely, in American slang

explanation.surface: Drinks first, then conversation: a gin and tonic to open a social evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gin and tonic' looks like one drink; split it after Gin, which is the definition in its sense of a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin, short for engine, is a snare for catching animals, which is exactly what a trap is.

clue.text: Position of first in field, not second notice phoned in

indicators.note: not second says the second letter of the phrase is to be dropped

blocks.note: whoever is first in a field of runners is in the lead

explanation.surface: A comment about who leads the race, then a notice called in by telephone.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the H from THE LEAD to get TELEAD. A tele-ad is an advertisement placed in a newspaper by telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists a tele-ad as an advertisement dictated to a newspaper over the phone, a notice sent by telephone.

clue.text: Plover trod green ’til flying (12, two words)

indicators.note: things flying are scattered through the air, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird walks over the grass until it takes off.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures the bird itself walking then taking off; 'flying' is the shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The ringed dotterel is a small plover, a wading shorebird with a dark band round its neck.

clue.text: Prince making mark in broadcast

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
M is the abbreviation for the old German mark

explanation.surface: A royal makes his name on television.
explanation.definitionFit: An amir, or emir, is a Muslim prince or ruler, so the title is a synonym for a royal son.

clue.text: Tease playfully making one bristle more than once

indicators.note: doing something playfully means not doing it straight, so the letters are toyed with and reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Teasing someone in jest makes them bristle repeatedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bristle' reads as a verb for getting annoyed, but it is the noun; 'more than once' makes it plural.
explanation.definitionFit: A seta is a biological bristle; its Latin plural is the word needed for several of them.

clue.text: Mourn about a term sadly, Dido’s end in pyre?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word wraps round what follows
sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so these letters are disordered
end asks for only the final letter of the name

blocks.note: to cry is to weep in grief
the fodder rearranged
the last letter of Dido

explanation.surface: Lamenting the end of a term, with Dido's death on her funeral pyre in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Aeneid Dido, deserted by Aeneas, dies on a pyre, so the surface evokes her lament. The question mark flags that a pyre is only an example of the thing defined.
explanation.definitionFit: A crematory is a place or furnace for burning the dead, and a funeral pyre served that purpose in ancient times.

clue.text: Cobras dead in water plant

blocks.note: Naia is a genus name for the cobras
D is the abbreviation for dead

explanation.surface: Snakes found lifeless in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in water' looks like a location for the dead snakes, but 'in' only links, and 'water plant' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Naiad is also the name of a genus of submerged aquatic weeds, besides meaning a river nymph.

clue.text: Insects sank (so it’s said) with age

indicators.note: so it's said tells us to go by the sound of the word rather than its usual spelling

blocks.note: dipped means sank, and dipt is an old spelling pronounced the same
an era is an age

explanation.surface: Insects went down in number as time passed.
explanation.definitionFit: Diptera is the order of two-winged insects, the flies, so the scientific name covers a large group of them.

clue.text: Kitchen essential maiden kept in range down under

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: in Tasmania a tier is a mountain range
M is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A young woman shut up in an Australian kitchen with its cooking range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' tempts as the stove that fits the kitchen; it is a line of mountains in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: A timer is a clock device used to measure cooking times, a standard piece of equipment for any cook.

clue.text: Pub device next to Scotch, we hear

indicators.note: we hear points to a word's sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: syne is the Scots word for next or then

explanation.surface: A gadget in a bar sits beside the whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' looks like whisky beside a pub device, but it means in the Scots language.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn's hanging sign carries a heraldic device, so the painted board outside a pub is its emblem.

clue.text: A hydrous sulphate, one found in Morocco?

indicators.note: found in says one piece is located inside the other

blocks.note: Morocco is a strong ale once brewed in Westmorland, so it is an example of the drink
a unit is a single thing, one

explanation.surface: A chemist identifies a mineral sample from North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Morocco looks like the country, natural beside a mineral; here it is an old strong ale, and the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Alunite is a mineral, a hydrated sulphate of aluminium and potassium, used in making alum.

clue.text: Naughty surprise upset p-priest – take pulse!

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the stammered word rearranged
R stands for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions
gram is a pulse, a type of bean or chickpea

explanation.surface: A cleric, stammering in shock at a saucy surprise, is told to check his heartbeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulse' reads as the heartbeat to take; it is a legume, and 'take' is the R from prescriptions.
explanation.definitionFit: A strippergram is a message delivered by someone who undresses, a risqué surprise booked for a party.

clue.text: Junior journo is in team, to help with grant

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a sub, short for sub-editor, is a junior newspaper journalist
a side is a team
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cub reporter joins the staff to assist with a funding application.
explanation.definitionFit: To subsidise is to support financially, giving money to a person or enterprise to keep it going.

clue.text: Tedious talk to make clumsy progress after time

indicators.note: after says the longer piece follows the other

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to waddle is to walk awkwardly, swaying side to side

explanation.surface: A boring speech drags on clumsily as time passes.
explanation.definitionFit: Twaddle is silly, pointless chatter, the kind of speech that bores the listener.

clue.text: Cancelled tenancy in legal document

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a deed is a signed legal instrument
a let is a lease of property

explanation.surface: A lease is struck out of a contract.
explanation.definitionFit: Deleted means struck out or removed, as an order or entry is when it is called off.

clue.text: Two measures (large then small), component of stiffeners

blocks.note: a bale is a large bundled quantity of goods
an en is a small printer's measure of width

explanation.surface: A recipe calling for one big quantity and one tiny one as part of the stiffening.
explanation.walkthrough: The parenthesis tells us the order of the two measures, big one first.
explanation.definitionFit: Baleen, or whalebone, was used to make corset stays and collar stiffeners before plastic.

clue.text: Volume to fail thus will make one sick

blocks.note: to vomit is to be sick
V is the abbreviation for volume

explanation.surface: A big dose of something makes a person ill.
explanation.walkthrough: Read in reverse: V plus the answer ('thus') makes VOMIT, so the answer is VOMIT without its V.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit to do something is to fail to do it, leaving it undone.

clue.text: Master that is holding children up for history error maybe

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from the bottom
holding means grasping inside, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for master, as in MA
i.e. is short for id est, that is
tads are small children

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster keeps pupils back over a mistake in history lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'history error' sounds like a wrong fact in class; it is a wrong date, and 'maybe' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: To misdate is to give the wrong date, the typical slip made when recording a historical event.

clue.text: Threshold that’s not well thought out, yard short

indicators.note: short means lacking, so the following letter is taken away

blocks.note: a silly idea is a foolish, ill-considered one
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: A doorway measurement badly planned, falling a yard short.
explanation.definitionFit: A sill is the slab at the bottom of a doorway, the step you cross on entering.

clue.text: Regular tried a little, second (or third) coming first

indicators.note: coming first says this letter is moved to the front of the word

blocks.note: to taste is to try a small amount of food
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A frequent customer sampled a bit, coming in second or third before being first.
explanation.walkthrough: The S is the third letter of TASTED, hence 'second (or third)': take it out and put it at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Stated means fixed or settled, as in meetings at stated intervals, which come at regular times.

clue.text: Last of tail, I’m out bowled, in the last period

indicators.note: last of asks for only the final letter of the following word
bowled means sent rolling, so these letters are tumbled into a new order

blocks.note: the final letter of tail
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricket tail-ender laments being bowled out in the final session.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the tail is the weak late batsmen; 'bowled' fits the scene but is the shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultimo is old business-letter Latin for last month, as in 'your letter of the 5th ultimo'.

clue.text: Woman with inner passion to keep under wraps?

indicators.note: with inner says the woman holds the other piece inside her

blocks.note: she is a woman
heat is intensity of feeling

explanation.surface: A woman hides the secret love she feels inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep under wraps' looks like keeping a secret; read literally it is putting something in a cover.
explanation.definitionFit: To sheathe is to put a blade into its scabbard, literally covering it up, hence the question mark.

clue.text: In chess I’m ultra displaying grandmaster’s stunt

indicators.note: displaying means showing within, so the run of letters is on view inside these words

blocks.note: found across the words chess, I'm and ultra

explanation.surface: A chess player boasts of being an extremist showing off a master's trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A simul is an exhibition where a grandmaster plays many opponents at once, a display of skill.

clue.text: Section of choir also unusually including tenor

indicators.note: unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters are reordered
including means taking in, so the shuffled letters surround the other piece

blocks.note: the word rearranged
T is the choir abbreviation for tenor

explanation.surface: One part of the choir oddly also includes a tenor.
explanation.definitionFit: The altos are the voice part between sopranos and tenors in SATB choral music.

clue.text: Here’s cardi styled, about time … thus?

definitions.text: Here’s cardi styled, about time … thus?

indicators.note: styled means arranged in a fashion, so the letters are restyled
about means surrounding, so the mix goes round the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written; cardi is short for cardigan
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone presents a cardigan put on in a muddle, and says it's about time.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a cardigan shuffled on in a hurry shows someone dressing absent-mindedly, and the scrambled letters themselves look that way.
explanation.definitionFit: Distractedly means absent-mindedly, as when someone buttons a cardigan askew while thinking of other things.

clue.text: Walter’s brother is brought up with young chaps’ organization

indicators.note: in a down entry, brought up means the word is read from the bottom

blocks.note: taken as written
BB is the Boys' Brigade, a Christian youth movement

explanation.surface: A man's brother was raised in a youth club.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter is Sir Walter Scott, who uses sibb, an old Scots form meaning a kinsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Sibb, related to sibling, means a relative in Scott's writing, so for him a brother is an example.

clue.text: Eye up European badgers as a group

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from the bottom

blocks.note: a private eye is a detective, a 'tec
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Continental eyes watch a group of badgers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eye up' looks like a phrasal verb for staring; split it, as eye is the detective and up the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cete is the collective noun for badgers, the way a group of them is named.

clue.text: Parody kept within limit, a tease

indicators.note: kept within says the letters are held inside the following words

blocks.note: found across limit, a and tease

explanation.surface: A satirical skit that holds back, a gentle ribbing.
explanation.definitionFit: To parody someone is to mimic them for comic effect, which is copying their manner.

clue.text: Local ruler, king attending university

blocks.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
to be at something is to attend it
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A regional chief and a monarch go to college together.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratu is a title for a chief in Fiji and parts of Indonesia, a ruler of a district.

clue.text: Cork, a teaser to twist

indicators.note: to twist means to turn round, so the word is read the other way

blocks.note: a rebus is a picture puzzle

explanation.surface: A tricky bottle stopper that needs a corkscrew to twist it out.
explanation.walkthrough: Cork looks like the Irish city or a stopper; it is the bark material.
explanation.definitionFit: Suber is the botanical name for cork tissue, the bark of the cork oak.

clue.text: To eat carefully, I avoided beef and cut out unhealthy stuff

indicators.note: avoided means kept out, so the letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: to diet is to eat with care for weight
taken as written
beef comes from an ox

explanation.surface: A dieter stayed off red meat and gave up junk food.
explanation.definitionFit: A detox is a period of purging the body of toxins by giving up harmful food and drink.

clue.text: Led sire out in run, second unmounted

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the letters are rearranged
in places the mix inside the other two pieces

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
the phrase rearranged
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A racehorse's father, led out for a run, came second without a jockey.
explanation.definitionFit: Riderless describes a horse with no one on its back, which is what unmounted means.
